processing_steps.method: vacuum induction melting under argon atmosphere; cast into ingot
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The steel was melted in a vacuum induction furnace under argon atmosphere and cast into ingot.
The ingot was forged to a thick slab.
Homogenization at 1200 °C for 2 h prior to hot rolling.
Hot rolled to 6 mm thickness after homogenization.

processing_steps.method: solution treatment / austenitization then water quench
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: HR plates were heated to 1050 °C, isothermally held for 0.5 h, quenched in water.
Cold rolled to 3 mm thickness (from 6 mm HR plate).

CR sheets annealed at temperatures from 600 °C to 1050 °C for 1–5 min then quenched in water; DP950-5 corresponds to 950 °C for 5 min. Specimens termed DPXXX-Y where XXX is annealing temperature and Y the period.

structures.overall_structure: Austenite-ferrite duplex microstructure formed by annealing the CR structure at 950 °C for 5 min: partially recrystallized austenite matrix (54.8 % Rex-γ) plus two types of ferrite (granular α ferrite and banded δ ferrite, total ferrite up to ~36 % by EBSD), together with Cr7C3 carbides and intergranular κ-carbides.
structures.number_of_phases: 5 constituents (austenite γ, granular α ferrite, banded δ ferrite, Cr7C3 carbides, intergranular κ-carbides)
structures.microstructure_counts: Rex-γ fraction 54.8 %; ferrite fraction by XRD 30.5 %; α ferrite by EBSD 23.8 %; δ ferrite by EBSD 12.1 % (total ferrite by EBSD ~36 %)

phases_present.morphology: partially recrystallized; annealing twins and shear bands present (Fig. 2c1)

microstructure_list.region: granular α ferrite (at austenite grain boundaries/triple points)

phases_present.morphology: granular; the granular α ferrite grains are coarsest in DP950-5 among the annealed specimens
phases_present.grain_size: coarsest among annealed specimens in DP950-5

microstructure_list.region: banded δ ferrite elongated along RD

phases_present.morphology: banded, elongated along the rolling direction; corresponding δ ferrite bands are the thickest in DP950-5 (Fig. 2c1)

microstructure_list.region: grain boundaries, BCC/FCC interfaces and ferrite bands

phases_present.morphology: two types: coarse particles of several micrometers located in ferrite bands, and particles of hundreds of nanometers precipitating at grain boundaries
formed at grain boundaries and BCC/FCC interfaces with coarse size of 2–3 µm in DP950-5

precipitates.distribution: at grain boundaries and BCC/FCC interfaces in DP950-5 (Fig. S2a)

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: The large amount of ferrite in DP950-5 causes incompatible straining at the many interfaces between ferrite and the unrecrystallized austenite due to the great difference in their strength/hardness, leading to easy initiation and propagation of cracks at/along the interfaces; hence poor ductility.

interfaces.phase_evolution: During annealing at 950 °C for 5 min: austenite → ferrite + Cr7C3 carbides + intergranular κ-carbides (austenite-to-ferrite transformation may occur during heating to 950 °C).
interfaces.interface_notes: The δ/γ interfaces behave differently depending on their orientation relative to the tensile axis; in DP950-5 the δ ferrite bands lie parallel to the RD (tensile direction along RD).

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: flat dog-bone-shaped tensile specimen, gage length 25 mm, length direction along the rolling direction (RD)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Uniaxial tensile tests; three tensile measurements were made for each heat treatment condition and the average values taken.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve for DP950-5 (cyan curve) shown in Fig. 3a; the curve rises steeply and terminates below about 7 % strain.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Measured by buoyancy balance according to Archimedes Principle

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: yield strength and ultimate tensile strength (effect of increasing annealing time at 950 °C from 1 to 5 min)

specific ultimate tensile strength (SUTS) versus total elongation compared with 2000 series Al alloys, Ti6Al4V, and existing duplex and austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels (Fig. 3b); 'Our steel' data points include DP950-5

characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification (austenite FCC, ferrite BCC, β-Mn, carbides) and determination of the ferrite fraction
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 950 °C condition, both κ-carbides and Cr7C3 carbides appeared (at 950–1000 °C); ferrite fraction of DP950-5 measured by XRD is 30.5 %.

characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with SAED and EDS
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Zone axis B = [0001] for Cr7C3 SAED; 200 nm scale bar bright-field image
characterization_methods.key_findings: TEM of DP950-5 (Fig. 1b) shows a chain of dark particles along a grain boundary (point ①) with a Cr-rich EDS map; SAED labelled 'Cr7C3 carbides' indexed (1̄100), (011̄0), (101̄0) at B = [0001].

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Phase (PH) mappings and grain-reference-orientation-deviation (GROD) mappings of austenite; dark lines are high-angle grain boundaries > 15°
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine phase fractions (α, δ, γ) and recrystallization (GROD < 2° criterion)
characterization_methods.key_findings: DP950-5 (Fig. 2c1/c2) shows the thickest δ ferrite bands; phase map predominantly yellow (advanced recrystallization) with black ferrite bands; α fraction 23.8 %, δ fraction 12.1 %, Rex-γ 54.8 %.

characterization_methods.purpose: Studying the mechanical response of different microstructural constituents
characterization_methods.key_findings: Nanoindentation results (Fig. S4, on DP1000-5) show that ferrite is clearly softer than the recrystallized austenite.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Strain rate 10^-3 s^-1, room temperature, flat dog-bone specimen gage length 25 mm, RD orientation

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Temperature range 550–1400 °C; the calculated ferrite fraction remains almost constant (~33 %) between 991 °C and 1250 °C and increases to a maximum when temperature decreases from 991 °C to 854 °C.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Measured ferrite fractions (XRD) are included for comparison; in contrast to the calculated maximum, the largest measured ferrite fraction appears at 900 °C, and measured ferrite fraction keeps decreasing above 900 °C, suggesting ferrite-to-austenite transformation.

unmapped_findings: DP950-5 specific strengths (Table 1): specific yield strength SYS = 144.7 ± 2.4 MPa·g⁻¹·cm³ and specific ultimate tensile strength SUTS = 212.3 ± 2.4 MPa·g⁻¹·cm³.

Products of SUTS and TE were reported to exceed 8 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·% for DP1000-5 and DP1050-1, while for 2000 series Al alloys and Ti6Al4V they are less than 4 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·%, and 2.7–6.5 and 2.9–7.4 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·% for duplex and austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels respectively; DP950-5 is one of the 'Our steel' red-star data points in Fig. 3b.

In the CR structure (prior to annealing), ferrite has two morphologies: granular ferrite at austenite triple points (0.6–1.8 µm) and band-like δ ferrite elongated along the RD (length 12–30 µm, thickness 2–6 µm); the δ ferrite is traced to the preceding HR/solidification structure.
β-Mn phase was detected by XRD at 700–900 °C but not at 950 °C (the DP950-5 annealing temperature).
